title: Dynamic Budget Reconsolidation & Contract Trigger Matrix
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document defines an operational framework for dynamically reconciling budgets and forecasts against contract events and procurement actions, and it provides a prescriptive trigger matrix that routes decisions (budget reconsolidation, legal review, procurement escalation, and revenue recognition hold/unblock) to the correct owners. The goal is to reduce surprise spend, ensure timely legal and revrec treatment, and shorten cycle time for enterprise deals and dedicated capacity contracts.

Scope:
- Applies to all commercial contracts and procurement commitments that impact: hosted API revenue, dedicated capacity commitments, private deployment commercial terms, and enterprise support packages.
- Covers forecast updates, mid-period reconsolidation, procurement approvals, contract amendments, and revrec recognition exceptions.
- Excludes small one-off purchases under the company petty procurement thresholds defined in the Procurement SOP.

Definitions:
- Reconsolidation: A forecast/reforecast pass triggered by a material contract or procurement event that requires updating plan and P&L burn allocations.
- Material event: Any contract or PO change that meets the thresholds in the matrix below (financial or operational).
- Deferred revenue hold: Temporary delay of revenue recognition pending legal/finance remediation (e.g., contract signature clarity, acceptance criteria unresolved).

Principles:
1. Single source of truth: Finance forecast (Adaptive Planning) is the canonical plan; all triggered changes must update the forecast within 3 business days.
2. Clear ownership: Triggers map to an owner_team and named owner for each action.
3. Minimal disruption: Apply staging & canary updates where possible (e.g., for multi-quarter dedicated commitments).
4. Auditability: Every reconsolidation must include an audit record (Jira ticket + linked contract ID).

Trigger Matrix (high level):

| Trigger type | Threshold | Immediate action | Primary owner | SLA | RevRec impact |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| New enterprise commitment (multi-year) | ARR >= $500k or TCV >= $1.5M | Create forecast reconsolidation ticket; legal intake for contract tiering; route to RevRec for timeline | Sales Finance Lead (owner) | 2 business days to open; 10 business days to reconcile | Deferred revenue schedule requires mapping on signature unless payment in arrears |
| Dedicated capacity commit increase | Monthly committed spend increase >= $200k | Trigger capacity-finance review; update reserved capacity budget line; procurement to confirm hardware commitments | Head of Capacity Finance | 3 business days | May create a capital/operating reclassification; coordinate with accounting |
| Amendment altering deliverables or acceptance criteria | Any change to acceptance terms or service-levels | Legal review required; product & services to confirm acceptance criteria; hold revenue until clarity | Contract Manager | 5 business days | Potential deferred revenue hold until acceptance criteria defined |
| Early termination/credit request | Refund > $50k or credit period > 2 months | Escalate to Finance Ops + RevRec; legal to validate termination clauses | Finance Operations | 3 business days | Revenue reversal and credit memos; revenue recognition impacted immediately |
| Procurement PO variance | PO change +/− 15% or > $100k | Procurement escalation; update vendor payment forecast | Procurement Lead | 2 business days | No direct revrec, but impacts cashflow forecasts |
| Change in billing cadence | Net change billing frequency (e.g., monthly->annual) | RevRec team to re-evaluate recognition timing and impact to deferred revenue; billing ops to update invoices | Billing Lead | 5 business days | Requires new revenue recognition schedule |
| Payment > 90 days overdue on large enterprise | Outstanding > $250k | Collections attempt; finance to model impairment; sales to engage customer executive sponsor | AR Lead | 3 business days to escalate | Consider reserve / bad debt assessment; potential rev rec reversal |

Operational Procedures (step-by-step):
1) Intake and Triage
   - Owner: Sales Finance Lead / Procurement Intake.
   - For any contract/procurement event that meets a threshold, create a Jira issue with labels: finance-recon, contract-trigger, <customer-id>. Attach contract excerpt or PO.
   - Triage team (Finance Ops + Legal rotation) must assign within SLA defined in the matrix.

2) Reconsolidation workstream
   - Owner: Forecast Steward (Finance).
   - Update the Adaptive Planning model: add new revenue/expense lines, annotate assumptions, and tag the change with the reconsolidation ticket ID.
   - Document scenario sensitivity: base, upside, downside using the standard sensitivity template (appendix A).
   - Notify FP&A and exec sponsors within 24 hours of model update.

3) Legal and Procurement coordination
   - Owner: Contract Manager / Procurement Lead.
   - If contract changes affect liability or acceptance, legal must prepare an amendment and checklist: signature path, counterparty representation, export controls, data residency clauses, and KMS/HSM references if applicable.
   - Procurement confirms vendor commitments, expected delivery dates, and any OPEX/CAPEX classification consequences.

4) Revenue recognition & Billing
   - Owner: RevRec Owner / Billing Ops.
   - Determine the recognition model: point-in-time, over-time (percentage of completion / service period), or contingent (deferred until acceptance). Attach journal template (appendix B).
   - If a deferred revenue hold is placed, generate a revrec hold memo and route to Accounting Manager for approval.
   - For prepayments or platform credits, ensure deferral schedules are created in ERP with appropriate GL mappings.

5) Closure and audit
   - Owner: Forecast Steward.
   - Close the reconsolidation ticket with a summary, impacted forecast lines, and links to signed contract documents. Retain a copy of the decision memo in the Finance drive and reference it in the internal audit log.

Roles & escalation paths (primary contacts):
- Forecast Steward: Lina Martinez, Sr. FP&A Manager (finance-legal)
- Contract Manager: David O’Malley (legal)
- Procurement Lead: Sophia Green (procurement)
- RevRec Owner: Ahmed Khan (accounting)
- Billing Lead: Nora Williams (billing ops)
- Exec escalation: VP Finance (for disagreements beyond owner remit)

Templates and examples:
- Reconsolidation Jira template (fields): customer_id, contract_id, trigger_type, threshold_hit, forecast_lines_impacted, expected_impact_usd, recommended_action, related_po_id.

- Example journal template (appendix B):
  {
    "contract_id": "C-2027-0453",
    "amount": "1500000",
    "billing_cadence": "annual",
    "recognition": "50000" /* monthly over 30 months */
  }

- Sample CLI snippet to export impacted forecast lines from Adaptive Planning (for automation):
  # export lines for contract C-2027-0453
  ap-cli export --model finance_forecast --filter contract_id=C-2027-0453 --format csv > /tmp/contract-0453-lines.csv

Change control and governance:
- Minor changes to thresholds (± 10%) may be approved by VP Finance; material changes to matrix (new trigger types or threshold doubling) require cross-functional steering committee approval (Finance + Legal + Procurement + Sales) and an update to this doc.
- Quarterly review cadence: Matrix is reviewed at FP&A monthly close and recalibrated quarterly based on actuals vs. forecast variance ranges.

Audit and compliance considerations:
- All reconsolidation tickets must include a copy of the signed contract/amendment or a link to Contract Repository ID.
- For revenue recognition decisions with material impact (> $250k impact in a quarter), obtain written sign-off from Accounting Manager and Legal Counsel before posting entries.
- Maintain retention in conformance with Finance Records Retention policy (minimum 7 years).

Appendix A — Sensitivity template (fields to capture):
- Assumption name
- Base case value
- Upside case value
- Downside case value
- Probability weightings
- Financial impact on ARR/TCV and cashflow by month

Appendix B — Standard journals and GL mappings (summary):
- Deferred revenue (contract liabilities): GL 2200
- Revenue recognized: GL 4000
- Customer refunds / credits: GL 5100
- Prepaid assets (where hardware CAPEX is managed): GL 1300

Appendix C — Quick decision flow (text diagram):
1. Event detected -> 2. Create reconsolidation ticket -> 3. Triage (Finance Ops + Legal) -> 4a. If contract/legal change -> Legal draft amendment -> 5a. If amendment affects revrec -> RevRec schedules -> 6. Update forecast and close ticket.
